answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a non-refundable admission bond, paid into a sable reserve, and requiring each newcomer to be countersigned by an established graph vertex. Mass-produced sockpuppets share near-identical behavior and form a disconnected island with no real inbound countersignatures. When clustering later proves one operator controls many accounts, the bond is burned and those identities lose attestation weight, so fake swarms cost more than they can earn.
